title: Sequentially Numbered Notes

illustrates.quote: Place notes at the end of the print page. a. Separate notes from text by a note separation line ⠰⠒⠒⠒⠒⠒⠒⠒ (5, 25, 25, 25, 25, 25, 25) across seven cells. The separation line cannot be on the last line of the braille page.

blocks.text: To my Lord's[ref:1] in the morning, where I met with Captain Cuttance. But my Lord not being up, I went out to Charing Cross to see Major General Harrison[ref:2] hanged, drawn, and quartered—which was done there—he looking as cheerfully as any man could do in that condition. …
blocks.features: Diary-style passage with print line number '15' at the left margin of its first line; two superscript numeral reference marks (1, 2) key sequentially numbered notes below.

blocks.text:
[ref:1] my Lord's: Edward Montagu (1625-1672), earl of Sandwich; he was a cousin of Pepys and his superior at the Naval Office.
[ref:2] Harrison: Thomas Harrison (1606-1660), one of the people responsible for the execution of King Charles I in 1649.
blocks.features: Two notes below a horizontal rule, numbered sequentially 1 and 2 in the order their marks appear in the passage above (not grouped by any other criterion).

notes.text: my Lord's: Edward Montagu (1625-1672), earl of Sandwich; he was a cousin of Pepys and his superior at the Naval Office.
Harrison: Thomas Harrison (1606-1660), one of the people responsible for the execution of King Charles I in 1649.

print.surroundingText: Cross-referenced from Example 16-7, illustrating rule 16.5.1c's sequential (not grouped) note numbering. This is a genuine excerpt: its braille line numbering begins at 15, not 1, matching the print passage's own starting line number.
print.printFeatures: Boxed screenshot of a diary-excerpt page, print line number '15' in the margin, horizontal rule, two numbered notes beneath.

pageBreaks.note: Explicit —New Braille Page— marker in the source, after braille line 25 (11th line of this excerpt, which starts mid-page at line 15); the line-number field restarts at 1 on the new page.

braille.notes: Genuine excerpt starting at braille line 15 (not line 1), verified on the page image -- no earlier lines invented. Line-number field width 5 (max line number 25, two digits, +3) used on both braille pages of this sample.

resolution: illustrates.rule set to 16.5.1 per standards-map.md's own BANA §16/B004 §11 worked-examples table (the project's established canonical id), not either run's own guess. print.blocks/print.notes follow Run B's schema ([ref:MARK] tokens inline + a separate print.notes[] array of {ref, placement, text}), matching this task's required schema; Run A instead folded each note's real content directly into a sibling print.blocks entry with no [ref:MARK] markers and always an empty print.notes[] -- a schema-level difference, not a content disagreement. braille.width: verified directly: lines 12960/12963/12969/12971/12974 (field width 5, digits(25)+3) are each exactly 40 characters after stripping the line-number field. braille.lines: the two runs agreed byte-for-byte; kept as transcribed.
